issues.body: The exact round-3 blocker remains: the README says the limits and timeout provide "the worst-case bound for embedded deployments." Cooperative cancellation/deadlines take effect only at an executor poll, and the added tests and skill explicitly acknowledge that index-answerable and tiny early-exit paths may finish before the first poll. Moreover, max_bytes accounts an estimated query working set rather than total process or window-materialisation memory. The skill repeats the same material overclaim as "the embedded-deployment bound" and describes a wall-clock bound even though it later states the polling limitation. A deadline checked cooperatively is not a strict wall-clock cap.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the README's worst-case-bound sentence and the corresponding claim in skills/streaming-rsp/SKILL.md with precise cooperative-limit wording. State that cancellation/timeouts apply at the next executor poll; max_bytes limits executor-accounted estimated working-set bytes, not total process or window-materialisation memory; and some bounded-work paths may complete before polling. Describe with_window_timeout as installing a refreshed per-evaluation deadline, not as strictly capping wall-clock duration.
issues.title: Public documentation still falsely promises a worst-case deployment bound

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant. The prior major honesty issue remains unchanged in the README, which still calls cooperative executor budgets and a timeout "the worst-case bound for embedded deployments." The skill now repeats the overclaim as an "embedded-deployment bound" and calls the relative deadline a wall-clock bound, despite correctly admitting later that polling is coarse and some paths complete before any poll. These APIs limit executor-accounted work only when polled; max_bytes is not total process/window-materialisation memory, and the timeout is not a strict wall-clock cap. The implementation and tests otherwise appear to exercise real budgeted prepared-query paths, but the public guarantees must be corrected before approval.
